question: On quotations taken from published English (and Hindi/Urdu/Bengali) translations that are NOT in the approved index, placed in neutral prose with no printed reference: does MIZAN locate them, identify the verse, and refer them (NEAR/UNATTRIBUTED) rather than falsely MATCH — and what does the semantic tier add on the same items?

protocol.verse_selection: second half of a seeded shuffle of all 6,236 verses (seed 20261003); tuning used the first half. Renderings of 8-90 words.

settings.in_prose: inserted at a sentence boundary inside a paragraph from the 120-paragraph false-positive probe (en/hi), which was never used for tuning
settings.bare: the rendering alone (ur/bn: no negative prose exists)

protocol.located: a finding whose verse id equals the true verse and whose span overlaps the inserted quotation
protocol.false_match: any finding overlapping the quotation in state MATCH; items whose text is literally in the index were excluded beforehand, so a MATCH here is false

selective_embedding_2026_10_04.what: 2026-10-04: tier (c) made fast on CPU without changing what it finds on any measured set. (1) Text the deterministic tiers already explained is not embedded. (2) Everything else is embedded in priority order within a per-request token budget (1,024 tokens): verse-like sentences, then pairs the model already placed confidently, then other sentences, then other pairs; drops are listed in last_semantic and logged. (3) The encoder uses batch 4 on CPU. (4) Two exact pruning bounds and a cached phase-1 seed remove repeated deterministic work. A first version used the verse-likeness gate as a hard FILTER: lossless on the English/Hindi/Tagalog dev split, but it lost Urdu/Tagalog/Bengali quotations on held-out and real text, so it was rejected; both are reported below. See docs/SEMANTIC.md §12.

latency_linux_container_4vcpu.how: deploy/experiments/bench_server.py (app.py over HTTP, model warm), Docker image mizan-bench (torch 2.14.1+cpu), --cpuset-cpus=0-3, MIZAN_DEVICE=cpu, 3 timed runs each. "before" = the previous detect.py mounted over the container copy with MIZAN_BATCH=32 (the old encoder default). "after_*" = the rejected gated plan. "budgeted_*" = what ships (three separate server starts for the 1,000-word article). "badload" = MIZAN_DEVICE=invalid_device: the model load fails once and is not retried per check (back-off). "det_*" = MIZAN_SEMANTIC=0. One first long check in budgeted_1000 was an outlier, see note_outlier. 1,000-word = deploy/experiments/make_docs.py long.txt (987 words, real article, 10 quotations); 2,501-word = that article + the most citation-rich other English islamreligion.com articles from data/real/raw, truncated at a paragraph boundary.
latency_linux_container_4vcpu.note_outlier: one first long check took 8.72 s (budgeted_1000 run 1); two further server starts gave 4.52 / 4.73 s for the first check, so it was not reproducible.

false_match_items_explained.why: The span located is "and give no thought to the life to come", verbatim the approved Salahi rendering of 75:21; Asad adds a bracketed gloss that stays outside the span. Tier (c) proposed the verse (augmentation), the lexical tier matched the words. An identical string, not prose attributed to an edition. The other 12 occur with or without tier (c); since report.py added partial attribution (2026-10-03) several are short clauses matched by partial attribution, three of them to a DIFFERENT verse that repeats the same formula (arberry 16:42 -> 29:59, ahmedali 38:72 -> 15:29, arberry 6:13 -> 26:220).

real_corpus_before_after.note: tests/real_corpus.py, unedited, with the CURRENT report.py in every run (its partial-quotation attribution changed states on 2026-10-03, so earlier runs are not comparable on states). budgeted vs previous code: 0 of 473 items differ in either condition; probe findings identical.

real_corpus_2026_10_03.note: tests/real_corpus.py, unedited, run three times. 'before' is detect.py as it was when this work started (snapshot kept outside the repo); 'after' is the deterministic path (plain python3, no ML packages); 'after_semantic' is the same harness under .venv/bin/python, where SpanDetector enables tier (c) by default.

dev_split.what: Tuning set, disjoint from everything above: 440 negative paragraphs NOT in the 120-paragraph probe; approved full / partial renderings and held-out editions (en.shakir, en.qaribullah, hi.hindi) of verses from the OTHER half of the seeded verse split, inserted into those paragraphs. Every threshold in detect.py was set here.
dev_split.note_on_negatives: Some 'negative' paragraphs contain real Quranic wording without quotation marks (verbatim 3:190, 85:22; a paraphrase of 84:8-9). The probe filter removed quote glyphs and references only, so part of every false-positive rate measured on these files is genuine unquoted scripture.

index_design_experiment.what: Retrieval only, on the dev split: 2,746 queries (held-out dev editions full and partial, plus real cited quotations with the citation stripped) and 1,410 sentences from dev negatives. 'R@1|neg1%' = top-1 correct AND scoring above the threshold that admits 1% of negative sentences — the operating point that matters, because a semantic span must be reported on the model's score alone.

designs.arabic: embed the 6,236 Arabic verses once; rely on cross-lingual alignment
designs.cent: per language, centroid of the approved renderings of each verse
designs.all: per language, every approved rendering kept separately (max per verse)

index_design_experiment.why: Best calibrated net gain over the centroid (+31) with a smaller index than any 'all' design: 6 x 12.8 MB float16 files instead of 190 MB for English alone, which also exceeds GitHub's 100 MB per-file limit for a repository that must be public.

reranker_experiment.what: Top-10 from the chosen index re-scored by the cross-encoder; 600 dev queries and 500 dev negative sentences; candidate text = the approved rendering in the query language closest to the query.
reranker_experiment.decision: Not used. It helps raw ranking only for partial quotations, hurts full ones, and is worse everywhere once it must also reject prose (its scores saturate near 1.0 on negatives). At 89 pairs/s, reranking 10 candidates for ~100 sentence chunks would add ~11 s per 1,000-word document.

build.machine: Apple M5, 16 GB, macOS, Python 3.11.0, MPS fp16

latency_12_documents_2026_10_03.what: The 12 longest real documents (mean 974 words), check_document end to end, one process, model warm. The machine was shared with a virtual machine using up to ~4 cores; the same code was timed three times and all three are reported.
latency_12_documents_2026_10_03.target: < 3 s for a typical 1,000-word document including the semantic pass
latency_12_documents_2026_10_03.verdict: median met in every run (1.86-2.82 s with semantic); the longest English document (1,271 words) is 3.2-4.6 s with semantic and does not meet it
